answer: In a sybil-resistant agent economy, membership requires surviving k-core pruning of the trust graph: only nodes with at least k mutually attested edges remain. A durable relic of each honest agent's attestation history proves it sits inside the dense core. Attackers spinning up falcon-fast clones pile into the graph's nadir, where sparse, one-sided links are pruned away, so their fakes never earn voting weight. Cost grows with genuine relationships, not cloned identities.
